title: Two-dimensional stealthy hyperuniform polycrystalline disk packings
authors: Carlo Vanoni, Paul J. Steinhardt, Salvatore Torquato
abstract: Polycrystals consist of grains of local crystalline order separated by grain boundaries. Their structure is not hyperuniform, even though perfect crystals are, because polycrystals consist of randomly sized and oriented grains that generate appreciable long-wavelength density fluctuations. In this paper, we use a collective-coordinate optimization procedure to generate two-dimensional polycrystalline packings composed of identical disks arranged in a pattern that is ultradense, stealthy, and hyperuniform (hereafter named SHU). We compare them with polycrystalline disk packings obtained via a modified Lubachevsky--Stillinger rapid compression algorithm (hereafter named LS), a molecular dynamics protocol that serves as a standard reference model describing realistic, nonhyperuniform polycrystalline microstructures. We carry out an extensive comparison of polycrystalline SHU and LS packings that includes differences in two-point statistics, grain size, specific surface area, diffusion spreadability, and optical response as quantified by the imaginary part of the effective dynamic dielectric constant. We find that the polycrystalline SHU packings exhibit a distinctive grain-size distribution, a consequence of long-range correlations between different grains that is absent in the nonhyperuniform case. Within the nonlocal strong-contrast expansion, we confirm that polycrystalline SHU packings made of dielectric material are perfectly transparent to electromagnetic waves at small wave vectors, in contrast to LS packings. Moreover, polycrystalline SHU packings offer enhanced diffusion spreadability. Although polycrystalline SHU packings are not expected to form spontaneously in nature, they may be created for applications as metamaterials via nanolithography or 3D printing that take advantage of their distinctive optical and transport properties.
summary: This work develops and analyzes two-dimensional Stealthy Hyperuniform (SHU) polycrystals using computational optimization. The SHU structures are shown to possess superior physical properties—including perfect low-frequency optical transparency and enhanced long-time diffusion—compared to conventionally formed disordered packings. This demonstrates a pathway to engineer functional materials by controlling density fluctuations in polycrystalline media.
main_problem: To generate and characterize two-dimensional polycrystalline packings that are ultradense, stealthy, and hyperuniform (SHU), contrasting them with standard models of polycrystals.
main_result: Polycrystalline SHU packings exhibit unique long-range correlations leading to perfect transparency at low wave vectors and enhanced diffusion spreadability compared to nonhyperuniform LS packings.
method: The study uses a collective-coordinate optimization procedure (CCO) to enforce stealthy hyperuniformity ($S(k)=0$ for $0 < k \le K$) in 2D disk packings, followed by comparisons of structural and transport properties.
model_or_system: The system consists of identical hard disks forming polycrystalline structures. The analysis compares SHU-generated packings against those from the standard Lubachevsky–Stillinger (LS) rapid compression algorithm, treating them as two-phase media (grains vs. boundaries).
key_observables: Structure factor $S(k)$, grain size distribution, diffusion spreadability $S(t)$, and the imaginary part of the effective dynamic dielectric constant $	ext{Im}(\epsilon_{	ext{eff}})$ for optical response.
important_parameters: Stealthiness parameter ($\chi$), wave vector ($k$), packing fraction ($\phi$), and characteristic length scales related to grain size.
main_assumptions: The SHU structures are idealized models not expected to form spontaneously in nature; the analysis relies on nonlocal strong-contrast expansions for optical response.
figures_summary: Figures compare spectral densities $	ilde{\chi}_V(k)$ showing zero weight at low $k$ for SHU vs. finite weight for LS, and plot grain size distributions highlighting a characteristic peak in SHU.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the concept of SHU packings via CCO optimization, compares their structural diagnostics (e.g., $	ilde{\chi}_V(k)$) against standard models (LS), and then analyzes functional properties like diffusion decay rates and optical transparency using established two-phase medium formalisms.
why_interesting: The ability to engineer macroscopic transport and optical properties (like low-$k$ transparency) by controlling the long-range density fluctuations in a disordered, polycrystalline structure is highly relevant for designing metamaterials and understanding complex condensed matter interfaces.

FIG. 2. (a) If all disks have six neighbors at distance d < dτ, with dτ defined in Eq. (21), they are assigned to a grain (blue). (b) Near a grain boundary, some disks satisfy this condition (disk 1, solid lines), while others do not and are assigned to the boundary (disks 2, 3, and 4, dashed lines).

FIG. 3. Grains (blue) and grain boundaries (red) for the same packing at different threshold values τ [Eq. (21)]. For small τ (upper left), no grains are identified. As τ increases, more disks are assigned to grains. For large τ, almost all disks are assigned to grains. We use τ = 0.08, where the grain–boundary interface is maximal.

FIG. 4. Grain–boundary interface length, averaged over 100 SHU configurations at ϕ = 0.86, as a function of the tolerance τ. At small τ, the average interface is near zero, consistent with the upper-left panel of Fig. 3. As τ increases, the inter- face increases and reaches a broad maximum plateau before returning toward zero at large τ. We choose the optimal tol- erance at the onset of this plateau (vertical red dashed line), namely τ = 0.08. The inset shows the same data on a log- linear scale.
